entries.reason: the port's bands run on an iPhone 4S and an iPad 2, and a reaction effect is a camera feature of the devices Apple shipped from 2016 on, so this camera has none of it: the 6.1.3 armv7 cache's AVCaptureDevice answers none of the reaction selectors either (tools/corpus/objc-inventory.lua), so no type is one that can be performed
entries.effect: raises NSInvalidArgumentException naming the selector and saying availableReactionTypes is empty. The header's rule is exact: "The reactionType requested must be one of those listed in availableReactionTypes or an exception will be thrown" (AVCaptureDevice.h:2496), and the list is empty here. The header names no exception for it; NSInvalidArgumentException is the name the two unsupported-argument refusals of this host's own class raise, measured
entries.source: the header of the SDK 26.2 (AVCaptureDevice.h:2485-2498), transcribed into CharonAVCaptureDeviceReactions17.h

entries.reason: the port's bands run on an iPhone 4S and an iPad 2, and a reaction effect is a camera feature of the devices Apple shipped from 2016 on, so this camera has none of it: the 6.1.3 armv7 cache's AVCaptureDevice answers none of the reaction selectors either (tools/corpus/objc-inventory.lua). The header's own words for the case are that the list is of the types that can be passed to -performEffectForReaction: and that it "may differ between devices"
entries.effect: an empty NSSet, the list for a camera that can perform none. Measured on this host's own camera: it answers all eight types, for the same reason it answers them - that camera has the hardware. An application that reads an empty set here knows it cannot ask for a reaction, and -performEffectForReaction: agrees

entries.reason: a CLASS property whose value "changes to reflect the Gestures state in Control Center" (AVCaptureDevice.h:2458), a setting no release of this port has, so what it answers is the documented default and the application's own override of it
entries.effect: YES by default - the header: "By default, gesture detection is enabled" (:2461) - and whatever NSCameraReactionEffectGesturesEnabledDefault in the application's Info.plist says from 17.4 on (:2462-2466). The host answers NO because it reflects this Mac's Control Center setting; a release with no such setting stays at its default, and gesture detection would do nothing here in any case because -canPerformReactionEffects is NO
entries.source: the header of the SDK 26.2 (AVCaptureDevice.h:2455-2466), transcribed into CharonAVCaptureDeviceReactions17.h; the default and the override both measured by tests/backports/host/avf-capabilities

entries.reason: a CLASS property about the application, not the hardware: the header's iOS rule is "enabled by default for video conferencing applications (apps that use \"voip\" as one of their UIBackgroundModes)", with NSCameraReactionEffectsEnabled in Info.plist as the opt-in for the others (AVCaptureDevice.h:2448-2450). Both are the application's own Info.plist, so both are read
entries.effect: YES when the application's Info.plist has UIBackgroundModes containing "voip" or NSCameraReactionEffectsEnabled true, and NO otherwise - the header's rule read through NSBundle, not a constant in either direction. It is the application half of the pair: what renders still needs -canPerformReactionEffects, which is NO here. The host answers YES because its own rule is "enabled by default for all applications" on macOS, which is another platform's rule
entries.source: the header of the SDK 26.2 (AVCaptureDevice.h:2437-2452), transcribed into CharonAVCaptureDeviceReactions17.h; both branches of the rule measured by tests/backports/host/avf-capabilities, which runs the port's own objects against four Info.plists

entries.reason: the camera the system prefers, which the header builds out of userPreferredCamera and "other factors, such as camera suspension and Apple cameras appearing that should be automatically chosen" (AVCaptureDevice.h:674); the other factors this release has are the ones its own +defaultDeviceWithMediaType: answers, and the port asks that function rather than naming a camera
entries.effect: the user's choice when there is one, and otherwise the release's own best camera, which on the devices of this port's bands is the one on the back; nil only with no camera at all. The host's own answer is nil here and is NOT Apple's answer for this row: this process's camera authorization is notDetermined, printed beside it by the harness, and a process that was never granted access answers nil
entries.source: the header of the SDK 26.2 (AVCaptureDevice.h), transcribed into CharonAVCaptureDeviceReactions17.h

entries.reason: the camera the user chose, which the header records as a class property with a setter and as persisting "across app launches and reboots" behind a "short history" (AVCaptureDevice.h:661-662); the release's own store is the system's and is not in the application's domain - measured on this host: setting the property adds 0 keys to the bundle's own defaults - so the port keeps the choice in the application's NSUserDefaults under the key CharonCaptureUserPreferredCameraHistory
entries.effect: the most recent entry of the short history that is in the list of connected cameras now, and never an entry that is not; nil while nothing was ever chosen, which is what the host answers too (measured); the release's own best camera once the history is exhausted, which is nil itself on a device with no camera; and a nil set adds nothing, so a choice made before it survives it (measured on the host: after setting nil the getter still answers the camera it was given)
entries.source: the header of the SDK 26.2 (AVCaptureDevice.h), transcribed into CharonAVCaptureDeviceReactions17.h
